images.caption:
Walking a section of the London Loop (London Outer Orbital Path) — at Buckhurst Hill. 
Part of section 19 of the London Loop. Running west-east across the middle of the grid square.
An ancient cattle drove, probably first used some 2000 years ago but the practice of driving livestock between pastures died out in the 19th century.

images.caption:
Earl's Path Pond in Epping Forest. 
This pond, the remains of 19th-century gravel workings, is beside the Earl's Path and the Three Forests Way
The larger pond further south at Strawberry Hill is surrounded by woodland. Much of the woodland here is not "ancient", but has recovered after clearances.

images.caption:
Queen Elizabeth's Hunting Lodge, Chingford, England, dates back to Tudor times, although it has been heavily altered over time.  The building is open to the public.
I took this photo myself and am releasing it into the public domain.  After all, I didn't design the building, so it seems morally wrong for me to claim any rights over its likeness.  Besides, it's not as if this is a very good picture anyway!
